_comment: NPC ships (docs/MASTER_DESIGN.md sections 6, 7 and 12). Each loadout lists the hull, engine, weapons and optional 'shield' and 'radar' (ids from equipment.json; ships without a radar get a basic one); the race that built them is the ship's race. Pirates: 'min_danger' (0-1) is how far from the races' home systems a loadout starts to appear ('danger' = distance to the nearest home system / danger_distance), 'hull_hp' is the share of armor they start with (pirates are battle-worn), 'bounty' is what the Ranger Corps pays for destroying one, 'cargo' is [min, max] units of goods they carry (part of it is left in the wreck, plus salvage). Traders: 'cargo' is [min, max] units on board and 'credits' [min, max] their trading money. Police guard the planets of systems with a government (how many: 'police' in world.json), patrolling within 'police_guard_distance' of them, and attack pirates that come within 'police_engage_distance' of a planet (wanted pilots anywhere in the system). Pirates come back with 'pirate_respawn_chance' per day, other ships with 'respawn_chance'. Rangers roam the galaxy hunting pirates ('ranger_count' of them).
_comms_comment: Hailing (game/sim/comms.gd). A bribe costs 'bribe_base' plus 'bribe_share' of your credits. Bribed, scared-off or paid-off ships leave you alone for 'truce_days'. A threat works when your fighting strength beats theirs times 'threat_ratio' times (0.5 + their race's courage). 'demand_share' and 'surrender_share' are the share of the hold handed over. Police and rangers only help against pirates within 'help_range' of them.
